newsitem.title: ITALY: MOTOR RACING-FERRARI BOSS SEES SCHUMACHER STAYING.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-FERRARI BOSS SEES SCHUMACHER STAYING.

text.p: Former world champion Michael Schumacher is set to stay at Ferrari after his contract expires next year, the company's president Luca di Montezemolo was quoted on Monday as saying.

Di Montezemolo was quoted by the daily La Stampa, owned by the Agnelli family which also owns Ferrari, as saying that Schumacher was almost certain to remain at the Italian Formula One team until after the 1998 season.
"Regarding Schumacher, we can practically guarantee another two seasons. Then we will see," he said.
"Bear in mind that, in Formula One, ties that go on for too long cause problems in the end. (Niki) Lauda, (Ayrton) Senna, (Alain) Prost all changed," he said.
Ferrari's honorary chairman Giovanni Agnelli said at the weekend that Schumacher would be staying.

Schumacher joined Ferrari in 1995 and helped the Italian team take second place in the Formula One constructors' world championship this season. He also won three races and finished third in the drivers' championship.
"Much of this was naturally due to Schumacher's ability," Agnelli told state broadcaster RAI. "He will stay at Ferrari for another two or three years."
Di Montezemolo said Ferrari had their sights set on the title in 1997 or 1998, preferably in 1997.
He said Schumacher had been signed at just the right moment for the team: "If we had signed him a year before that it maybe would have been a mistake. A waste."
